gates.title: Per-image licensing, archive capture, and public availability
gates.claim: ASSET_PLAN.md:117 lists 'Pexels, Pixabay (browsable without login)' as sources for hands shuffling cards; ASSET_PLAN.md:109-122 treats free stock as browsable without login.
gates.finding_on_plan_claim: Partly false for the agent on 2026-09-15. Pixabay search pages were browsable but held no suitable shuffling clip. Pexels individual video pages were not browsable by the agent (HTTP 403; Cloudflare verification interstitial). Mixkit, which the plan did not name, was browsable without login and supplied all three candidates.

per_candidate.rights_holder_creator: Mixkit (Envato); no individual creator named on the page
per_candidate.file_specific_terms: Asset page: 'Download this free stock video clip for commercial or personal use, under the Mixkit Stock Video Free License.'
per_candidate.access_method: Public asset page, no login; download not performed
per_candidate.open_risk: Printed casino felt layout visible (third-party table design, unbranded as far as seen). Terms s.13 (via WebFetch summary) says components such as trade marks may come from third parties and are the user's responsibility.

gates.license_evidence_quality: The license modal text was read directly from the rendered page DOM (class license-modal__inner) on 2026-09-15. The User Terms limits come from a WebFetch model summary of https://mixkit.co/terms/ (reported 'last revised October 2, 2025') and were not read verbatim.
review_questions: Taste: is the printed casino-table felt in rank 1 (100384) acceptable for a family card game (War) segment, or should the plain-felt rank 2 (100398) lead despite its 0.5 s handles and flourish-style motion?
Legal risk: are visible card-back and table-layout designs (possible third-party components under Mixkit User Terms s.13) acceptable without further clearance?
Boundary: approve the batched download of rank 1 Full HD (70.51 MB), or all three (173.39 MB), per exports/acquisition-handoff.md?
Evidence: is the WebFetch summary of the Mixkit User Terms sufficient, or should the Terms be read verbatim before release?
